neighbours.label: the hero's-journey / monomyth frame of myth and story structure (call to adventure, quest, trials, mentor, archetypes, Campbell)
fire: In many myths, the hero must cross a threshold into an unknown world.
Campbell called this pattern the monomyth, the story behind all stories.
Before the journey begins, the mentor figure gives the hero a magic gift.
Like Gilgamesh, the hero returns from his quest changed forever.
Many screenwriters follow the hero's journey when they plot an adventure film.
The epic describes the trials the prince endures on his road to the underworld.
Jung's archetypes include the trickster, the shadow and the great mother.
After refusing the call, the reluctant hero finally accepts his destiny.
quiet: In many cities, the bus must cross a bridge into the old town.
The author called this book her favourite of all her novels.
Before the semester begins, the teacher gives each student a folder.
Like his father, the plumber returns from every job tired and dirty.
Many screenwriters follow a tight schedule when they film a cheap comedy.
The report describes the delays the project endured on its way to completion.
The museum's collection includes paintings, coins and old maps.
After a long delay, the reluctant buyer finally signed the contract.
